correctness.rationale: The exact two-scalar divisibility criterion follows from Cayley--Hamilton and A^3=abA. Explicit q_t,p_t factorizations establish all initial valuations; lifting from an entry of exact 2-adic valuation at least two forces one unit of valuation per doubling. Finite-reduction kernel is a 2-group and therefore the displayed order is minimal. A union-of-proper-subgroups argument proves the exact maximum individual orbit length. Replay independently verified 490 modular matrix orders, 2250 scalar comparisons and 407376 finite states, without treating those finite tests as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact order of a finite symplectic torus automorphism is a natural dynamic recurrence invariant. The theorem resolves it for all complete-bipartite graph couplings and every 2-power modulus, including parity thresholds and genuinely nontrivial valuation plateaus. Same-product graph pairs have distinct exact orders, so graph shape matters and the calculation is not a scalar 2x2 deduction; a maximum primitive orbit is also proved to occur.
